matching_rule: A candidate matches a line's expected description when EVERY token of the expected description is present in the candidate name's token set. Both sides are normalized identically: NFD-decompose and strip diacritics, lowercase, replace non-alphanumerics with spaces, drop stopwords (with, and, of, the, a, an, in, on, for), and singularize each token (trailing 'oes' -> 'o', trailing 'ies' -> 'y', otherwise a trailing 's' is dropped unless the token ends in 'ss' or has length <= 3). Matching uses the candidate NAME only (brand is recorded in the results but is not part of the match). The rule is printed verbatim in the probe report; lines whose correct real-world entry the rule cannot express carry an `ambiguity` note here.
provenance: Built 2026-11-11 for the S3 receipt-correlation probe (model-integration brief, seat S3). The 28 item lines are copied verbatim from fixtures/receipt-eval/expectations.json (hand-labelled from the three Commons receipt photos, CC BY-SA 4.0): raw_label, name, is_food, quantity and unit are the labelled extraction ground truth — no fresh extraction is run. The 6 trap lines are the non-item lines the receipt-eval notes record as printed in frame (subtotal/amount/cash/tax/count on the ALDI receipt, the 'Aktie!' discount line on the Coop receipt); extraction never emits them, so each trap entry's `name` duplicates its printed label and the probe feeds the printed label as the search text. Shortlists are generated at runtime from the production food search, so `expected` is a plain-language description of the correct database entry, matched against candidate names by the deterministic rule below.
